problems.title: The positive-entropy leading resonance is false for the specified scalar operator
problems.source_section: Problem 1: positive entropy is not a scalar leading resonance
problems.location: Theorem F p.7; scalar resolvent p.41; Theorem 12(3) p.47; Theorem 13(3) p.51; distinction from form lifts on p.43.
problems.claim_refuted: For U=0, positive topological entropy is the leading scalar Ruelle resonance of A=-X on the admissible compact example.
problems.decisive_evidence: A faithful torsion-free cocompact surface-group lift in SL(2,R) is irreducible and projective Anosov. Its limit set is RP^1 and M=K is compact PSL(2,R) quotient. Invariant contact volume makes exp(tA) unitary on L2. The negative Laplace integral for (A-lambda)^(-1) is holomorphic for Re(lambda)>0. Constants exhibit a pole at zero. The positive entropy is therefore not a scalar pole.
hypotheses: Dimension and group

V=R^2 satisfies d>1. A closed genus at least two oriented hyperbolic surface has faithful holonomy lift avoiding -I because the Euler class is even; projection is injective, hence the subgroup is torsion-free.
Projective Anosov and irreducibility
Cocompact Fuchsian translation lengths control stable word length and the two eigenvalue moduli give the gap. No real invariant line exists for this non-elementary lattice.
Assigned domain and basic set
The full RP^1 limit set makes every transverse pair admissible, so M=K=Gamma-bar\PSL(2,R), a compact manifold. This compact case is expressly admitted on source p.3.
Potential and operator
U=0 is smooth and compactly supported on the compact manifold, and A=-X is exactly the scalar operator specified.
Resolvent and entropy

Contact volume is finite and invariant; composition by the flow is unitary. The right-half-plane resolvent integral is analytic. The flow is the positive constant time rescaling of a compact hyperbolic geodesic flow and has h>0.
problems.impact: A headline spectral conclusion and its entropy-state interpretation fail for the operator actually stated.
problems.impact_limit: This example does not refute exponential mixing, meromorphic zeta continuation, or the geometric construction.
problems.repair: Specify the appropriate differential-form degree, any orientation twist, pairing and open-system extension; or change the scalar potential and prove the altered pressure/regularity claims. A global resolvent sign change cannot move poles. A merely Holder conjugacy does not automatically transport wavefront-defined distribution products.
problems.severity_reason: Repair changes the spectral object or potential in a main theorem, rather than a local normalization. The compact admissible counterexample contradicts the claimed pole directly.
problems.calculation_role: Decisive independent analytic semigroup argument; no numerical pole-detection claim.

problems.title: The allowed cyclic case has two periodic components and a double zeta pole
problems.source_section: Problem 2: the cyclic boundary has two periodic components
problems.location: Theorems A/B pp.3-4, D p.6; Proposition 2.9 p.13, Definition 2.14 p.14; Theorem 2/Lemma 3.12 pp.22-23; elementary sentence p.25; Theorem 6 p.39; one-dimensional application ranges pp.47,51.
problems.claim_refuted: The canonical full refraction flow is transitive with one basic component, and its zeta function has a simple leading pole, for every non-trivial torsion-free projective Anosov group as literally allowed.
problems.decisive_evidence: Gamma=<diag(2,1/2)> satisfies the stated gap. Its two ordered boundary pairs are fixed separately and each flow fiber quotients to a circle of period log(2). The two primitive conjugacy classes are g and g^(-1), so zeta(s)=(1-exp(-s log(2)))^(-2), with a double pole at entropy zero.
hypotheses: Group range
Infinite cyclic is non-trivial, torsion-free, finitely generated and hyperbolic; non-elementarity is not in these literal statements.
Gap and limit maps
Stable word length of g^n is |n| and eigenvalue-log gap is 2|n|log(2), satisfying c=c'=log(2). The primal maps are e1,e2 and the corresponding dual maps are e2*,e1*, giving cross-pair transversality.
Periodic identification
Both ordered endpoint pairs remain distinct under this abelian action. Each real fiber quotients by translation of absolute size log(2). Both g and g^(-1) are primitive and nonconjugate.
One-dimensional application
The positive projective interval is properly strictly convex under the stated definition, its Hilbert quotient is compact, and its unit sphere bundle consists of the two oriented periodic circles.
problems.impact: Literal elementary-range transitivity and simple-pole assertions fail; one-dimensional mixing assertions also need a range restriction.
problems.impact_limit: The example is reducible and does not refute the intended irreducible non-elementary mixing theorem. Theorem A's existential choice alone is not claimed to exclude a different domain selecting one component.
problems.repair: Add non-elementarity where used, or state the cyclic two-orbit case separately. Retain needed irreducibility/dimension qualifiers in applications.
problems.severity_reason: A localized range correction, with the intended non-elementary arguments unaffected by this counterexample.

problems.title: A relative sign sends the pseudo-hyperbolic map outside its target
problems.source_section: Problem 3: the pseudo-hyperbolic embedding has the wrong sign
problems.location: Positive-pairing target p.44 and displayed map Phi_partial^(p,q+1) p.45.
problems.claim_refuted: The map [x:v] -> [x+v:x-v] lands in the stated positive-pairing space.
problems.decisive_evidence: With B(x,x)=-1, B(v,v)=1 and B(x,v)=0, the printed pairing B(x+v,x-v)=-2. For p=2,q=0 take B=diag(1,1,-1), x=(0,0,1), v=(1,0,0). Common projective rescaling cannot change the sign.
hypotheses: Permitted signature
p=2,q=0 is within the stated range.
Unit spacelike tangent domain
The explicit x,v have B(x,x)=-1, B(v,v)=1 and B(x,v)=0.
Target and quotient
The target requires positive B(v1,v2); both entries have one common projective scaling, so the negative pairing cannot be removed by an allowed common rescaling.
problems.impact: The displayed map does not take values in its declared target.
problems.impact_limit: No counterexample to the intended geometric mixing conclusion is claimed.
problems.repair: Use [x+v:v-x] with the consistent inverse [v1-v2:v1+v2] and common unit normalization. The geodesic equations then give the required e^t/e^(-t) scaling.
problems.severity_reason: An explicit local sign repair restores the intended construction.

problems.title: The printed residue is the negative projector and the initial half-plane ignores the potential
problems.source_section: Problem 4: resolvent residue and starting half-plane conventions
problems.location: Section 5.2 and Theorem 9 p.41; spectral-parameter convention in Theorem 10 p.42.
problems.claim_refuted: Res_(lambda=c)(A-lambda)^(-1) is a projection, and the scalar L2 resolvent is initially defined on all Re(lambda)>0 for every allowed potential.
problems.decisive_evidence: On the same admissible compact example with smooth constant U=c>0, A1=c1 and (A-lambda)^(-1)1=(c-lambda)^(-1)1. The residue acts by -1, so (Pi^2-Pi)1=2, and lambda=c>0 is a pole.
hypotheses: Compact admissible example
All geometric and group hypotheses are the same verified ones as P001.
Allowed potential
The real constant c>0 is smooth; its support is compact because the ambient manifold is compact.
Exact operator convention
The computation uses precisely the stated A=-X+U and (A-lambda)^(-1), on its invariant constants.
problems.impact: Projector normalization and the claimed starting domain are incorrect. The quoted -iX counting strip also needs rotation to the -X parameter.
problems.impact_limit: Pole locations and ranks survive a global resolvent sign correction. The citation/convention mismatch is not a separate counterexample to every printed counting bound.
problems.repair: Use -Res(A-lambda)^(-1), or (lambda-A)^(-1); start in Re(lambda)>sup Re(U) with invariant volume. For P=-iX use lambda=-iz, so Re(lambda)=Im(z), and invoke the open-system counting statements with their hypotheses.
problems.severity_reason: Localized sign and domain conventions; the distinct main scalar-entropy issue is P001.

problems.title: The local-product point need not belong to the basic set for an arbitrary ambient base point
problems.source_section: Problem 5: the local-product claim needs a basic-set restriction
problems.claim_refuted: For every ambient y near x in K, the local stable/central-unstable intersection lies in K.
problems.decisive_evidence: For a torsion-free classical Schottky subgroup of SL(2,R), the stable intersection with K has a Cantor endpoint parameter. Choose y arbitrarily near x on its local stable leaf but outside K. Since y is on its own central-unstable plaque, the unique local intersection is y, which is outside K.
hypotheses: Section 4 group hypotheses
A classical torsion-free Schottky group is non-elementary, irreducible in the standard representation, convex cocompact and projective Anosov.
Base point and neighborhoods
Take x in K and choose y in the local stable leaf inside the prescribed ambient ball and domain; openness and the nowhere dense Cantor endpoint set permit this for every sufficiently small radius.
Ambient plaque and uniqueness
The analytic ambient stable and central-unstable plaques are defined at y. It belongs to both Ws(x) and Wcu(y); their local-product intersection is unique.
problems.impact: The ambient quantifier in the lemma is false.
problems.impact_limit: Subsequent uses already restrict to the basic set, so this does not refute the intended holonomy or mixing conclusion.
problems.repair: Require y in K intersected with the small ball. Clarify that item (5) parallel transport is along the leaf where it was defined.
problems.severity_reason: A local quantifier repair matching later usage.
problems.calculation_role: Independent geometric counterexample; no numerical experiment required.

checks.source_claim: Theorem F, source page 7; scalar resolvent setup and Theorems 9-11 on pages 41-43; positive-entropy applications on pages 47 and 51.
checks.independent_reasoning: A torsion-free cocompact Fuchsian surface group has a faithful lift to SL(2,R): the oriented surface Euler class 2-2g is even, and the lifted representation projects faithfully. It is irreducible, and the uniform eigenvalue gap relative to stable word length makes it projective Anosov under Definition 2.14. Its limit set is all RP^1. Definition 3.6 and the inclusions on pages 20-21 therefore give Ktilde=L and M=K=Gamma\PSL(2,R), a compact quotient explicitly permitted in the introduction. Normalize alpha(v)=1 and choose w in ker(alpha) with det(v,w)=1. The common-sign projective quotient identifies [v:alpha] with the class of the matrix (v,w); the flow is right multiplication by diag(exp(t),exp(-t)). It is the geodesic flow with twice the usual curvature-minus-one time and has entropy 2>0. The Reeb flow preserves the finite contact volume, so T_t f=f composed with phi^(-t) is unitary on L2 and has generator A=-X. For Re(lambda)>0, (A-lambda)^(-1)=-integral_0^infinity exp(-lambda t)T_t dt is a holomorphic bounded L2 operator, with norm at most 1/Re(lambda). Its composition C-infinity -> L2 -> distributions is holomorphic there, so uniqueness of meromorphic continuation excludes a pole at the positive entropy. Constants instead give (A-lambda)^(-1)1=-1/lambda and a pole at zero. This is an admissible exact compact counterexample, not a numerical search for poles.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: Source page 41 explicitly restricts the discussion to scalar functions and says lifts to vector bundles are not considered there. The later mention of appropriate differential forms in the zeta argument does not change Theorem F's specified scalar operator. Humbert distinguishes the leading scalar pressure P(V+J^u) from P(V) in the relevant stable form degree; in this example J^u=-2, so the scalar leading pressure is zero and the form pressure is the positive entropy. Dyatlov-Guillarmou also permits the compact case and places the zero-potential scalar resonance at zero. A resolvent sign convention changes residues, not pole locations. Repair requires a different bundle degree/orientation convention and its pairing/open-system justification, or a different scalar potential; a merely Holder flow conjugacy cannot automatically pull back arbitrary wavefront distributions. The central scalar spectral conclusion and its positive-entropy identification are materially wrong, supporting Major without alleging failure of the geometric construction, intended mixing, or zeta statements.

checks.source_claim: Definition 2.14 and Lemma 2.11, pages 13-14; Theorems A-B, pages 3-4; canonical basic set and transitivity, pages 20-23; elementary discussion, page 25; zeta definition and simple-pole claims, pages 5-6 and 39; one-dimensional application range, pages 43-47 and 51; introductory applications, pages 8-9.
checks.independent_reasoning: For Gamma=<diag(2,1/2)>, stable word length is |n| and the first eigenvalue gap of g^n is 2|n|log(2), so the stated projective-Anosov inequality holds. The group is nontrivial and torsion-free; the definition does not exclude a virtually cyclic group, which Lemma 2.11 even explicitly addresses. Its two boundary points give two ordered transverse endpoint pairs. In the Hopf parameterization each is a separate periodic component of period ell=log(2), so their union has no dense orbit and is not one transitive basic set. The two primitive conjugacy classes g and g^(-1) are distinct in this abelian group. Hence the source's Euler product is zeta(s)=(1-exp(-ell*s))^(-2), entropy is zero, and lim_(s->0) s^2*zeta(s)=ell^(-2): the asserted simple pole is a double pole. The properly convex interval in RP^1 has Hilbert coordinate distance one-half the logarithm of the endpoint ratio; the quotient is a circle of length ell and its oriented unit bundle has two periodic components, whose nonconstant Fourier observables do not mix.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The cyclic example is reducible and therefore does not contradict the explicitly irreducible intended mixing theorem C. It does contradict the broader canonical identification/transitivity and simple-pole statements where only nontrivial torsion-free projective Anosov is assumed. Theorem A alone is existential, so the report correctly uses its combination with the prescribed full refraction flow/canonical basic set rather than claiming every possible open domain must retain both circles. BCLS explicitly excludes the virtually cyclic case, and section 4 of the source supplies non-elementarity locally; that later assumption does not retroactively narrow the earlier statements. The Hilbert/pseudo-Riemannian introductory formulations need the corresponding non-elementary/dimension and irreducibility qualifications. Minor is a localized statement-range repair; it is not evidence against the intended non-elementary irreducible results.

checks.source_claim: Pseudo-hyperbolic domain and target definitions, pages 44-45; printed forward map and inverse, page 45.
checks.independent_reasoning: An admissible normalized pair satisfies B(x,x)=-1, B(v,v)=1, B(x,v)=0. Therefore B(x+v,x-v)=-2, while the target requires a positive pairing. Under the source's common projective rescaling this pairing is multiplied by a square and its sign cannot change. The concrete signature-(2,1) choice x=(0,0,1), v=(1,0,0) satisfies every displayed domain condition and exhibits the obstruction. Replacing the second component by v-x gives pairing +2. The corresponding inverse [v1:v2] -> [v1-v2:v1+v2] has B(x,x)=-2B(v1,v2), B(v,v)=+2B(v1,v2), and B(x,v)=0, and both compositions are the common factor 2. The corrected map sends the cosh/sinh geodesic formula to the required exp(t), exp(-t) factors and is equivariant.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: An independent sign change of one target component is not the source's common projective equivalence, so it cannot rescue the printed formula. The report's paired forward/inverse correction works and is local; no failure of the underlying flow conjugacy or mixing theorem is inferred. Minor is appropriate.

checks.source_claim: Resolvent convention, initial half-plane and residue projector on page 41; copied counting strip on page 42. Dyatlov-Guillarmou reference pages 3-6 and Jin-Tao reference pages 1-4.
checks.independent_reasoning: On the same allowed compact example let U=c>0. Smooth compact support is permitted because M=K is compact. Then A1=c and (A-lambda)^(-1)1=(c-lambda)^(-1). Its residue at lambda=c acts as -1 on constants; its square acts as +1, so the displayed residue is not a projector. The same positive pole disproves an initial inverse on the entire half-plane Re(lambda)>0 for arbitrary U. With A=-X+U and this resolvent convention the spectral projector is minus the residue and a safe initial half-plane depends on the growth bound, for example Re(lambda)>sup Re(U) in the invariant-volume setting. Dyatlov-Guillarmou instead writes (Xdg+lambda)^(-1), with Xdg=X-V, a positive Laplace integral, and a potential-dependent initial growth bound; its positive Laurent projector cannot be copied without changing the sign. Jin-Tao uses P=-iX. Since A=-X=-iP, lambda=-iz and Re(lambda)=Im(z): their horizontal Im(z)>-beta resonance strip becomes a right Re(lambda)>-beta half-plane in A's convention.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: Jin-Tao's open-system and global Axiom-A statements have their own assumptions, and the report does not use a coordinate translation alone as a counterexample to every possible resonance count. The exact constant-potential/eigenspace checks establish the residue and initial-domain errors. Repairing these conventions leaves P001's positive-entropy scalar error intact. Minor is appropriate for this separate normalization/domain issue.

checks.source_claim: Stable foliation on page 27; Lemma 4.3(3), page 28; basic-set restriction in Definition 4.4, page 29; Stoyanov LNIC/local-product setup, reference page 7.
checks.independent_reasoning: Take a torsion-free non-elementary Schottky subgroup of SL(2,R), which is irreducible and projective Anosov and has a Cantor limit set. In the source's endpoint description K requires both endpoint coordinates in the appropriate limit sets. The local stable leaf fixes the primal endpoint and varies the dual coordinate. For x in K, choose arbitrarily close y on that stable plaque with dual endpoint outside the Cantor limit set; the open ambient domain still contains y but K does not. Then y lies both on the local stable plaque of x and on its own local center-unstable plaque. By the source's unique ambient local product, their intersection is y, outside K. Lemma 4.3(3) quantifies over arbitrary ambient y in the stated small ball and therefore has a false K-membership conclusion.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: Restricting y to K in that ball restores the standard local-product assertion. Definition 4.4 already uses x,y in K and separately notes that the transported point belongs to K exactly when its original point does; Stoyanov likewise states the local-product conclusion for x,y in the locally maximal set. The example meets section 4's non-elementarity assumption and does not assert failure of the ensuing intended basic-set argument or exponential mixing. Minor is a quantifier correction.

checks.verdict: retain NeedsEvidence; not promoted to a supported Problem
checks.source_claim: Definition 4.19, Lemmas 4.20-4.21 and Theorem 3, source pages 34-37; Stoyanov reference page 7.
checks.independent_reasoning: The strong displayed condition chooses one d0>0 before every small epsilon. Lemma 4.20 supplies compact-uniform constants for each fixed delta. In Lemma 4.21 epsilon is chosen first, then a delta fitting that epsilon, then d0(delta); this proves a fixed-scale angle and supplies no positive lower bound uniform as epsilon shrinks. The fixed-scale temporal logarithm/transport estimate was checked and does not by itself reverse those quantifiers. Stoyanov's weaker original LNIC has different tangency/base-point allowances but still makes its cone choice before the subsequent small-scale quantifiers.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: No independent counterexample to the intended mixing theorem or to the needed weaker condition has been established. A separate uniform-angle argument or a direct check of Stoyanov's original hypotheses could resolve the gap. The report accurately treats this as unresolved evidence, not another Major/Minor mathematical defect.
